in-entacmaea-quadricolor.title: Bubble Tip Anemone
in-entacmaea-quadricolor.summary: An anemone with bulb-tipped tentacles that swell when it is fed and stretch out when hungry. It relies on light for much of its food and anchors its foot deep in rockwork.
rows: About 12 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 40 cm (15.7 in) across (SeaLifeBase)
With caution (LiveAquaria). Give it room away from corals in a mixed reef
Carnivore. Gets part of its food from symbiotic algae, so it needs strong light; also feed meaty foods
Indo-Pacific: Micronesia and Melanesia to east Africa and the Red Sea and from Australia to Japan
notes: Needs a large, established tank with strong filtration and skimming; it can reach about 12 in across.
Moderate to high light and medium flow suit it.

in-epicystis-crucifer.title: Rock Flower Anemone
in-epicystis-crucifer.sci: Epicystis crucifer (also listed as Phymanthus crucifer)
in-epicystis-crucifer.summary: A colorful Caribbean anemone that buries its column in sand or a rock crack so only the disc shows. Hardy and rarely wanders.
rows: With caution (LiveAquaria). Rarely wanders once settled
Carnivore. Feed small pieces of mussel or other fresh seafood
Caribbean Sea and West Indies; sandy bottoms with the column buried
notes: Adapts to a wide range of lighting. Can be kept singly or in groups.
Wild disc size is up to about 6 in (15 cm) across.

in-macrodactyla-doreensis.title: Long Tentacle Anemone
in-macrodactyla-doreensis.summary: A sand anemone with long, often corkscrew-shaped tentacles and a red base. It buries its foot in sand or rubble.
rows: Carnivore. Small pieces of fish or mussel, crustaceans and frozen foods
notes: Needs about 4 in of sand or rubble to burrow into.
Moderate light and medium flow suit it.
